summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: RNA World hypothesis states that RNA was the primordial genetic material and catalytic enzyme (Ribozyme). DNA evolved through 2'-deoxy modification and Thymine substitution for superior chemical stability. tRNA acts as an adapter molecule: 2D Cloverleaf model (3'-CCA acceptor, Anticodon loop, DHU loop, TpsiC loop) folding into a tertiary 3D L-shape.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THE RNA WORLD HYPOTHESIS
                                         │
   RNA evolved as the primordial genetic material AND biological catalyst (Ribozymes).
                                         │
   DNA evolved from RNA through 2'-deoxy modification and Thymine substitution,
   conferring superior chemical stability and double-stranded repair mechanisms.
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 Chemical Stability: DNA vs. RNA
1. **$2'$-Hydroxyl Group ($2'\text{-OH}$)**: RNA contains ribose with a reactive $2'\text{-OH}$ group, making RNA chemically labile, reactive, and susceptible to alkaline hydrolysis. DNA contains $2'$-deoxyribose, conferring higher stability.
2. **Uracil vs. Thymine**: Uracil in RNA is susceptible to spontaneous cytosine deamination ($C \rightarrow U$). DNA utilizes **Thymine (5-methyluracil)**, allowing cellular repair systems to recognize deaminated cytosines as abnormal.

### 2.2 Structural Classes of RNA

```
                                  RNA CLASSES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
   MESSENGER RNA (mRNA)          RIBOSOMAL RNA (rRNA)          TRANSFER RNA (tRNA)
   ├── 1--5% total RNA           ├── 80% of total cellular RNA ├── 15% total cellular RNA
   ├── Short-lived template       ├── Structural & Catalytic    ├── Adapter molecule (73--93 nt)
   └── Monocistronic/Polycistr.       (Ribozyme: 23S/28S)       └── Cloverleaf 2D / L-shaped 3D
```

### 2.3 The Transfer RNA (tRNA) Adapter Molecule

```
                          tRNA CLOVERLEAF vs L-SHAPE
                          
        2D CLOVERLEAF MODEL                        3D L-SHAPED MODEL
        
          3'-ACC-5' (Acceptor)                         3'-Acceptor
             │                                            │
        ┌────┴────┐                                       │
        │ TψC Loop│ ──► Binds Ribosome                    │
        └────┬────┘                                       │
             │                                            ▼
        ┌────┴────┐                                 Anticodon Loop
        │ DHU Loop│ ──► Binds Synthetase
        └────┬────┘
             │
      [Anticodon Loop] ──► Binds mRNA Codon
```

- **Functional Sites of tRNA**:
  1. **$3'$-Acceptor Stem**: Unpaired terminal **$5'\text{-CCA}-3'$** sequence; amino acid attaches covalently to the $3'\text{-OH}$ of the terminal Adenylate.
  2. **Anticodon Loop**: $3$-nucleotide sequence complementary to the mRNA codon.
  3. **DHU Loop (D-Loop)**: Contains dihydrouridine; recognized by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase.
  4. **$\text{T}\psi\text{C}$ Loop**: Contains ribothymidine and pseudouridine; binds the large ribosomal subunit.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Ribozymes and Catalytic RNA
conceptBreakdown.title: Ribozymes and Catalytic RNA
conceptBreakdown.content: Ribozymes (such as 23S rRNA peptidyl transferase, RNase P, and self-splicing Group I/II introns) demonstrate that polynucleotide chains can fold into tertiary catalytic conformations to accelerate biochemical reactions without protein enzymes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase Proofreading
conceptBreakdown.title: Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetase Proofreading
conceptBreakdown.content: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases possess a two-sieve proofreading mechanism: the activation site excludes amino acids larger than the correct substrate, while the hydrolytic editing site destroys mischarged smaller amino acids.
